newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end softer, fall on financials.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end softer, fall on financials.

text.p: Downward corrections on the most heavily weighted financials pulled Taiwan share prices to a slightly lower close on Saturday, brokers said.
At one stage the weighted index rebounded to a high of 7,190.66, but weakness in the financial sector saw it close 19.22 points or 0.27 percent lower at 7,154.20.
Turnover was an active T$55.88 billion.
"Profit-taking on financials prevented a possible rebound, but plastics' emerged as a bellwether sector to support the market," said Yuanta Securities analyst Henry Chen.
First Commercial Bank ended down T$3.00 at T$173.00, but plastics shares rose 0.73 percent on recent raw material price increases. Taiwan Styrene Monomer was up T$1.70 to T$38.20.
"Plastics had consolidated for eight months, and I believe it's time for the sector to launch a major rebound," Chen said.
Chemical and construction counters rose, but electronics fell.
Brokers said they expected the market to consolidate in the week ahead as the six-year resistance at 7,200 points remains a critical barrier.
A 7,000-7,250 range is seen in the week ahead.
